description: An aged, wrinkled hand holds a brass pen or compass-tipped stylus over a parchment map crossed with red and blue rhumb lines. A compass rose sits lower left and a small camel with a rider lower right, near a fragment of coastline. On the left are bowls of red, blue and yellow pigment and brushes in a jar, in a dim timber-beamed stone room. No text, numbers or frame are visible, and nothing is graphic.
reason: Shows a hand drawing rhumb lines on a map beside pigment bowls, with a camel rider, but the card is the 1381 killing of Wat Tyler at Smithfield. Nothing of that parley or the rising appears.
